lines.text: Well, {managerA} has an equal claim to the conversation, but not to the crown. Nobody gets that.
{managerB} finishes exactly level overall, and suddenly the loudest person in our studio has gone quiet.
At the end of the entire Showdown, the argument survives. The contest itself is officially drawn.
Funny how {clubA} can finish with precisely the same total and still leave us so much to debate.
Nobody has lifted the overall title, but both managers have earned a proper seat at this desk.
As for {clubB}, even the fiercest case for superiority collapses under the finished totals. Nobody's ahead.
lines.was: For {clubB}, that's an equal finish across the full contest. Try finding a fairer final verdict.

lines.text: You can pack away the predictions now. The complete Showdown has ended with no manager ahead.
Somebody ordered a championship celebration, and the standings sent back a very polite refusal.
Ask {managerA} for the overall lead, and the standings answer on behalf of the rival. Nobody has it.
lines.was: {managerA} can point to the final tally all evening. So can the other manager, of course.

lines.text: Look at the overall totals. No champion, no runner-up, and absolutely no shortage of opinions.
Those closing figures have settled the competition without settling a single studio argument.
{clubA} ends the rivalry's competition on equal terms. That's a formidable conclusion, not a consolation.
What a gift for the scriptwriters. A grand finale with a cast that refuses to sort itself into first and second.
lines.was: This has the feel of a grand finale, except the script refuses to pick a leading role.

lines.text: If {managerB} expected the last word, there's a catch. It belongs to both sides.
The final ledger gives neither club the upper hand, and for once the panel can't disagree.
There's no trophy presentation for an overall champion here. Just a rivalry that refused to bend.
Put every season together and the managers stay inseparable. That ending has earned its own place in the archive.
lines.was: Every season is finished, every total is final, and the managers are still standing level.

lines.text: Watching {clubB} finish shoulder to shoulder is a reminder that equality can make a cracking ending.
So the Showdown closes without a champion. It turns out a shared ending can still make headlines.
Neither the upper hand nor the lower step belongs to {managerA}. The complete Showdown ended square.
lines.was: {managerA} hasn't been beaten overall, and hasn't beaten the other manager either. That's the whole story.

lines.text: Can someone explain how we spent all that time arguing only to finish with a perfectly shared verdict?
{clubA} gets the same overall return as its rival. Even our resident contrarian respects that.
No need to cut this verdict into smaller pieces. The full competition ended completely even.
You want a decisive finale? Sorry, the managers have delivered something considerably more awkward for pundits.
Quite a finish for {managerB}, who reaches the final page with nothing between the overall totals.
Here's the uncomfortable part for our predictions. Both sides were equally right at the end.
In an ordinary debate, somebody wins. In this Showdown, not even the closing figures choose sides.
{clubB} has matched the opposition's overall tally. There's a difference between sharing and surrendering.
Every confident prediction has met a small but important obstacle. The final result is tied.
lines.was: Everyone picked a favourite. The final standings appear to have declined every single invitation.

lines.text: Apparently the grand prize today is permission to argue about this rivalry for as long as you like.
For {managerA}, the best rebuttal is already printed. Not a point separates the closing totals.
lines.was: {managerA} has an impeccable answer to any claim of overall superiority. The totals are identical.

lines.text: A handshake would suit this finish better than a podium. Neither manager stands above the other.
Take another look at {clubA}. The overall balance remains exact, even after the last season.
Try separating these managers with a ruler. You'll only end up measuring your own stubbornness.
lines.was: We've had the entire Showdown to separate them. The finish has chosen not to cooperate.

lines.text: Good luck asking {managerB} to concede bragging rights. There's nothing in the totals to concede.
Our panel was promised a final verdict. What we received was a beautifully stubborn dead heat.
There's {clubB}, matching its rival at the finish. Even the fiercest critic must call that even.
lines.was: {clubB} can take equal pride from this contest, and the rival club can say precisely the same.

lines.text: Leave the champion's chair empty and fill the studio with theories. What a fitting way for a tie to end.
lines.was: There won't be a champion's chair tonight. Perhaps that's why both managers still look so comfortable in the story.

lines.text: I'm prepared to admit something unusual. The tie is more interesting than half our predictions.
Our boldest predictions have met their natural predator. {managerA} and the rival finish level.
lines.was: {managerA} ends level, and the only thing trailing behind is the credibility of our confident forecasts.

lines.text: We could flip a coin, but that would be our game, not the Showdown's result.
{clubA} and {clubB} end on matching overall points. Even the studio's arguments have reached a stalemate.
Someone call the engraver and tell them to put the pen down. No sole champion emerged.
You know what suits {managerB}? Finishing without being outdone, and without outdoing the rival either.
The closing credits have rolled, and neither manager's name gets a bigger font.
Let's congratulate the rivalry. It has somehow managed to win the argument against all our predictions.
{clubB} holds its end of the bargain. Across the whole Showdown, there is simply no separation.
I came armed with a winner's speech. The completed Showdown has politely handed it back.
lines.was: Honestly, that's a wonderfully inconvenient result for anyone who came here looking for a loser.

lines.text: With a straight face, the finished totals deliver their closing joke. Neither side finishes higher.
lines.was: One final check of the totals, and the conclusion stays the same. Equal all the way home.

lines.text: Give {managerA} full credit for an even finish. Then turn around and do likewise for the rival.
lines.was: {managerA} can leave this contest with a straight back. So can the manager across the divide.

lines.text: Give {clubA} the top line and somebody will ask why its rival is missing. Fair point.
lines.was: In the end, {clubA} gets no higher billing than its rival. That's accuracy, not stinginess.

lines.text: Picture the final graphic, {managerB} level with the opposition. The producers couldn't design a neater argument.
If our studio had a vote, it would still change nothing. {clubB} has ended level with its rival.
lines.was: I'd love to announce a champion, but {clubB} and the opposition have made that impossible.

lines.text: I'd love a solo champion on the studio screen. {managerA} and the opposition have other ideas.
lines.was: Spare a thought for our predictions desk. {managerA} has just rendered half its paperwork unnecessary.

lines.text: Listen, the final whistle is shared, figuratively speaking. Neither side gets the last laugh.
lines.was: The Showdown has reached its full stop, while the debate keeps reaching for another sentence.

lines.text: Draw a line through the closing figures and you'll find {clubA} sitting squarely beside its counterpart.
lines.was: There's a place for {clubA} in this story, and it's exactly alongside the other club.

lines.text: Not many finales leave {managerB} with an equal standing and the commentators still searching for a verdict.
We've called it from every angle. {clubB} cannot be separated from its rival in the final reckoning.
A headline writer asked who took the title. {managerA} has brought an inconveniently symmetrical answer.
lines.was: Normally the closing montage has a leading character. {managerA} has an equally important counterpart.

lines.text: In the final edition, {clubA} must share the front page. No editor could choose otherwise.
lines.was: The last page is written, and {clubA} shares the headline rather than taking it alone.

lines.text: Well played to {managerB}, and equally well played to the manager who matched that total.
{clubB} has reached the same destination by the end. Nobody gets the exclusive map.
A mischievous little twist for {managerA}. The last comparison is an exact reflection.
lines.was: That final graphic is almost mischievous. {managerA} has exactly as much to claim as the rival.

lines.text: I'd say {clubA} deserved the overall crown, but the opposition can make the very same case.
If {clubB} had hoped to stand alone, the completed standings have offered a more communal ending.
lines.was: Now here's a proper talking point. {managerB} finishes neither above nor below the other manager.

lines.text: Call it a split decision and you'd be wrong. {clubB} has no greater claim than its rival.
lines.was: {clubB} shares the ending, and it's rather a good one for a rivalry built on comparison.

lines.text: Maybe our studio should declare itself drawn as well. We've certainly argued enough to earn it.
From opening debate to closing graphic, {managerA} ends with exactly as much as the rival.
lines.was: {managerA} has matched the rival all the way to the final tally. That's staying power.

lines.text: Side by side in the final record, {clubA} and its rival become an editor's spacing problem.
lines.was: Consider the balance here. {clubA} could not break away, and neither could the other side.

lines.text: We asked for a winner of the whole thing. {managerB} and the opposition supplied a perfect tie.
When {clubB} asks for the last word, the rival has an equally good claim. I love this.
lines.was: Even the last word is shared. {clubB} gets a mention, and the rival deserves one too.

lines.text: Ask anyone in this studio to pick a winner. Then ask them to explain the actual ending.
lines.was: On the evidence of this finale, {managerA} won't need a speech to defend that standing.

lines.text: The result offers {clubA} something better than a boast. A claim its rival can match word for word.
lines.was: That's a fine overall return for {clubA}. The catch is, the other club finished level.

lines.text: Neither manager owns the ending, which gives the rivalry an unusually satisfying symmetry.
The rivalry has delivered a final answer nobody can dispute. Neither manager is ahead.
lines.was: Try putting {managerB} on the lower step of a podium. The final result simply won't allow it.

lines.text: Whichever way you tilt the graphic, {clubB} stays level. Our director may need a new trick.
lines.was: {clubB} has no reason to look up at its opponent. The overall standings put them together.

lines.text: Someone in the studio still wants a winner. {managerA} can direct them straight to the equal totals.
I wouldn't call this unfinished business. {clubA} has completed the Showdown on identical terms.
This isn't a dangling plot thread. {clubA} has finished level, and the Showdown is finished too.
lines.was: A competition can end without selecting a champion, and {managerB} has helped prove it in style.

lines.text: Cue the ledger, not the victory speech. {clubB} has the same overall return as its opponent.
lines.was: The rivals have closed their accounts. {clubB} finds the same final figure on the other side.

lines.text: Picture the podium, then erase the higher step. {managerA} and the rival belong on equal footing.
lines.was: No dramatic reveal of a champion, just {managerA} and a rival who refused to be separated.

lines.text: Here's the archive's dilemma. Where do you file {clubA} when the entire Showdown has ended without a sole champion?
lines.was: Here's a rarity for the archive. {clubA} has finished a complete Showdown without an overall victor.

lines.text: An equal ending for {managerB} keeps the argument alive without deciding superiority.
lines.was: Everything has been decided except who is better overall. For {managerB}, the answer is neither.

lines.text: An equal share of the closing spotlight suits {clubB}. There's no reason to dim either side.
Our panel's farewell gift to {managerA}? An argument that survives the final whistle.
lines.was: We're left with an odd luxury. {managerA} can celebrate a fine contest without claiming superiority.

lines.text: A shared finish for {clubA} sounds modest until you remember the whole rivalry ended that way.
Someone has mislaid the champion's envelope. Then again, {managerB} and the rival made it unnecessary.
lines.was: The champion's announcement has been cancelled by mutual excellence. {managerB} won't be filing a complaint.

lines.text: An engraver could draw a line between {clubB} and its rival's totals. There wouldn't be a slope.
lines.was: Put {clubB} on the same line of the final record as its opponent. That's where it belongs.

lines.text: I've got a theory about {managerA}, but the equal standings have spoiled the dramatic conclusion.
Which name goes first in the caption? For {clubA}, that's the only question left to our graphics desk.
lines.was: Your final image is {clubA} alongside its rival, with neither name printed above the other.

lines.text: Well, {managerB} gets a share of the praise, and the opposition gets precisely the same.
Our graphics team loves a dramatic reveal. {clubB} keeps producing the same total as its rival.
lines.was: The overall scoreboard has a sense of humour. It gives {clubB} the same answer as everybody else.

lines.text: You could argue for {managerA} forever, but the matching totals aren't open to cross-examination.
lines.was: You could argue for {managerA} until closing time, and the rival's total would still match.

lines.text: At the finish, {clubA} and the opposition have written a joint ending neither can improve upon.
Put {clubA} beside its opponent on the closing graphic. Even our loudest pundit can read that.
lines.was: I like a conclusion that respects both managers. This one does it without inventing a champion.

lines.text: {managerB} doesn't leave with the title, but the other manager doesn't have it either.
Every pundit came looking for a gap. {clubB} has left us examining the space where one ought to be.
lines.was: Every pundit wanted a defining difference. {clubB} has left us a defining equality instead.

lines.text: Somebody ask for the simplest headline. {managerA} finishes level, and neither manager can claim the crown.
lines.was: Perhaps the fairest headline is the least flashy. {managerA} has ended completely level overall.

lines.text: Frame those closing totals however you please. No picture gives either manager the crown.
lines.was: There's no grand reveal to argue over. {clubA} and its rival have earned equal billing.

lines.text: Call the final outcome a tie, not a disappointment. This Showdown managed a rare, complete balance.
